finding.claim: With default config, any attacker-supplied https:// URL in Markdown is fetched server-side by the embed library (SSRF to internal hosts or cloud metadata), since the domain filter is only applied when embed.allowed_domains is non-empty.
finding.source: Attacker-authored Markdown line consisting only of an https:// URL (e.g. https://169.254.169.254/ or an internal hostname). Precondition: EmbedExtension registered with default embed.allowed_domains = [].
finding.sink: Embed\Embed::getMulti() outbound HTTP request in OscaroteroEmbedAdapter::updateEmbeds, line 43.

trace.note: Only check on the line is that it starts with 'https://'; host and IP are not restricted.
LinkParserHelper::parseLinkDestination extracts the attacker URL, which must be the whole line (line 47).
EmbedParser is created with the attacker URL and attached as an Embed block.
DocumentParsedEvent listener collects top-level Embed nodes and calls $this->adapter->updateEmbeds().
embed.allowed_domains defaults to [].
DomainFilteringAdapter is wrapped only when allowed_domains !== [] (lines 39-41). With the default, the raw adapter is used.
getMulti() fetches each URL. Nothing in this repo restricts private IPs, link-local addresses, or redirects.

finding.guards_checked: (1) https:// prefix check at EmbedStartParser.php:34 does not limit host or IP. (2) DomainFilteringAdapter.php:35-61 is not applied when allowed_domains is empty (EmbedExtension.php:39-41). (3) No private, loopback, or link-local IP check exists in src/. Verdict: CONFIRMED for default configuration; severity depends on whether the consumer renders untrusted Markdown.

finding.claim: Embed HTML returned by the remote site is emitted into output without escaping, so an attacker-controlled page can inject script into the rendered document (stored XSS via third-party content).
finding.source: Attacker-controlled remote page at an https:// URL on its own line, whose oEmbed/meta-derived HTML contains script or event handlers. Precondition: EmbedExtension enabled and allowed_domains empty or permissive.
finding.sink: Raw return of $node->getEmbedCode() from EmbedRenderer::render, line 33, with no escaping and no sanitization.

trace.note: Attacker URL becomes an Embed block.
Adapter takes $extractor->code->html from the fetched remote page when code !== null.
setEmbedCode() stores that HTML on the node with no transformation.
render() returns getEmbedCode() directly as the output string, so it is not HtmlElement-escaped like other nodes.

finding.guards_checked: (1) The adapter does not escape or sanitize the returned HTML (OscaroteroEmbedAdapter.php:46). (2) EmbedRenderer.php:33 does not escape. (3) No sanitizer or html_input filter applies to embed output; html_input is applied only to HtmlBlock and HtmlInline nodes (HtmlBlockRenderer.php:46, HtmlInlineRenderer.php:46). (4) allowed_domains limits which hosts can be used, but any allowed host, including one a user can publish to, supplies the HTML. Verdict: CONFIRMED by code reading; exploitability depends on the allow-list and on the consumer's trust in embedded hosts.

finding.claim: The allowed_domains check validates only the original URL. If the embed library follows HTTP redirects, an allow-listed host that redirects can send the server to an arbitrary internal or external host.
finding.source: Attacker Markdown line with an https:// URL on an allow-listed domain that serves or redirects to an attacker-chosen host (open redirect, user-content host, or a host the attacker controls).
finding.sink: Server-side fetch performed by the embed library after the filter has passed the URL (OscaroteroEmbedAdapter.php:43, reached via DomainFilteringAdapter.php:37).

trace.note: updateEmbeds() filters the embed list before the decorated adapter runs.
isAllowed() inspects only $embed->getUrl(), the original string.
Host matched exactly or as a subdomain of an allowed domain, so the filter passes.
Passing embeds go to OscaroteroEmbedAdapter, which fetches them. Redirect targets are never re-checked in this repo.

finding.guards_checked: (1) Scheme restricted to http/https (DomainFilteringAdapter.php:44-49). (2) Host compared exactly or by subdomain suffix (lines 51-58), which blocks look-alike hosts such as evil-example.com. (3) Redirect behavior of the embed library is not in this repo and was not verified. Verdict: PLAUSIBLE; confirm the vendored embed/embed version follows redirects and does not re-validate.

finding.claim: allow_unsafe_links defaults to true, so javascript:, vbscript:, and file: link destinations from untrusted Markdown are rendered as href values by default (stored XSS in clicked links).
finding.source: Attacker Markdown such as [x](javascript:alert(document.domain)), <javascript:alert(1)>, or ![x](javascript:...) with default config.
finding.sink: href attribute written by LinkRenderer::render (LinkRenderer.php:49), emitted as HTML.

trace.note: Default allow_unsafe_links = true.
forbidUnsafeLinks = !config(allow_unsafe_links) = false by default.
Unsafe check is skipped because forbidUnsafeLinks is false.
Raw $node->getUrl() written into href.

finding.guards_checked: (1) RegexHelper::isLinkPotentiallyUnsafe (RegexHelper.php:239-247) strips tab/LF/CR and leading control bytes and blocks javascript|vbscript|file|data, allowing only data:image/(png|gif|jpeg|webp). It is consulted only when allow_unsafe_links is false. (2) ImageRenderer.php:50-52 applies the same gate and is also off by default. (3) AttributesHelper.php:172 applies the same gate to {href=} and {src=} attributes, also off by default. (4) Output is escaped with Xml::escape, but that does not stop a javascript: scheme. Verdict: CONFIRMED as a default-configuration exposure; this is documented CommonMark default behavior, so it is a hardening issue for consumers rendering untrusted input.

finding.claim: html_input defaults to ALLOW, so raw HTML from untrusted Markdown is emitted unmodified, enabling script injection with default settings.
finding.source: Attacker Markdown with raw HTML, e.g. inline or an HTML block containing
finding.sink: Unfiltered output of HtmlBlock/HtmlInline literals (HtmlFilter::filter returns $html unchanged for ALLOW, HtmlFilter.php:49-50).

trace.note: html_input default HtmlFilter::ALLOW.
Reads html_input from config.
HtmlFilter::filter($literal, ALLOW) returns the raw literal. The block renderer does the same at HtmlBlockRenderer.php:46.

GFM adds DisallowedRawHtmlExtension, which rewrites only 9 tags (title, textarea, style, xmp, iframe, noembed, noframes, script, plaintext) at DisallowedRawHtmlRenderer.php:48-51. Other tags, including img, svg, object, and a, pass through.

finding.guards_checked: (1) html_input option supports STRIP and ESCAPE (HtmlFilter.php:45-48), but neither is the default. (2) GFM tagfilter (DisallowedRawHtmlRenderer.php:48-51) is a partial deny-list, not a sanitizer, and is applied only when that extension is enabled. (3) No HTML sanitizer exists in the library. Verdict: CONFIRMED as a default-configuration exposure; this is the documented CommonMark raw-HTML behavior, so it applies to untrusted input only when consumers keep the default.

finding.claim: With an empty attributes.allow list, the only attribute filter removes on* names. Other attributes an author can set via {...} pass unchecked (style, srcdoc, formaction, id, and xlink:href, for example), which allows CSS injection and DOM clobbering. Script execution is not shown.
finding.source: Attacker Markdown attribute block such as {style=...}, {#name}, or {formaction=...} on a paragraph, heading, link, or image. Precondition: attributes extension enabled with the default empty allow list.
finding.sink: Attributes merged into rendered HtmlElement output for the block or inline node (HtmlElement.php:130).

trace.note: Attribute block parsed from author-supplied text.
Name and value stored without a name allowlist beyond the name regex.
Names must match PARTIAL_ATTRIBUTENAME. This blocks malformed names but not dangerous well-formed ones.
With an empty allowlist, the only check is str_starts_with(name, 'on') at line 180.
Value is passed through Xml::escape (Xml.php:31), so quotes cannot break out of the attribute.

finding.guards_checked: (1) Name regex at line 164. (2) on* removal at line 180. (3) Value escaping at HtmlElement.php:130 and Xml.php:31, which blocks attribute breakout. (4) href and src unsafe-scheme check at line 172 applies only when allow_unsafe_links is false. Verdict: low severity; no script execution path was found in this repo, but the filter is weaker than its comment suggests.
